sections.skill: Explain automation bias and keep human judgment and responsibility

questions.prompt: What is automation bias?

choices.text: Trusting an automated suggestion too much
Refusing to use any automated system

questions.correct_answer: Trusting an automated suggestion too much
questions.intro: AUTOMATION BIAS is the tendency to trust an automated system's suggestion too much, even when other evidence says it is wrong. Examples: following a GPS into a lake, or approving every AI-flagged item without looking. Keeping HUMAN AGENCY means you stay the decision-maker: you understand the task, check important suggestions, and can explain your choices. RESPONSIBILITY stays with people, and DEPENDENCE grows when skills go unused, so practice key skills yourself sometimes. AI help is most useful when it supports judgment rather than replacing it.

sections.skill: Compare automation bias with relying on spell-check

questions.prompt: Why do people stop proofreading?

choices.text: Because proofreading is not allowed in schools or workplaces once spell-check is turned on

questions.intro: Spell-check catches many mistakes, so people stop proofreading. But it misses correctly spelled wrong words: "their" for "there," or "pubic" for "public." Someone who relies on it completely sends embarrassing errors. Someone who uses it AND reads their work catches more. AI help is similar: a useful tool, but trusting it completely lets its mistakes through.

sections.skill: Counter automation bias with design and habits

questions.prompt: Why is automation bias stronger when a tool is usually right?

choices.text: The rare error is easy to miss
Because accurate tools never make any errors at all, so there is nothing to check

questions.correct_answer: The rare error is easy to miss
questions.intro: Automation bias grows with fatigue, time pressure and high system accuracy: if a tool is right 99 times, the 100th error is easy to miss. Design and habits can help: require a reason before accepting high-stakes suggestions, show the evidence behind them, rotate tasks, and periodically do work without the tool to keep skills fresh. Reasonable people differ on how much to rely on AI in different areas; the core point is to choose deliberately.
